gloss: It is obvious without needing to say.
teaser: Today, we explore an idiom that highlights the clarity of understanding without words.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Today, we explore an idiom that highlights the clarity of understanding without words.[break 1s]The phrase is: 不言而喻, bù yán ér yù.[break 0.5s]不 (bù) - not[break 0.5s]言 (yán) - to speak[break 0.5s]而 (ér) - and[break 0.5s]喻 (yù) - to understand[break 1s]So, 不言而喻 literally means 'not speaking and understanding'. Figuratively, it implies that something is so clear that it doesn't need to be explained.[break 1s]Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s]This idiom originates from ancient times when scholars would often discuss philosophical ideas. They believed that some truths were self-evident and did not require elaboration. The phrase captures the essence of those moments when understanding is instant and clear without the need for words.[break 1.5s]Example 1: 这道题的答案不言而喻。 [break 1s]The answer to this question is obvious. [break 1s]Example 2: 他们的友谊不言而喻。 [break 1s]Their friendship is clear without needing to say a word. [break 1s]Example 3: 这件事情的结果不言而喻。 [break 1s]The outcome of this matter is evident. [break 1s]So, 不言而喻 means it is obvious without needing to say. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
